newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta share index drops four points, turnover up.
newsitem.headline: Malta share index drops four points, turnover up.

text.p: The Malta stock exchange share index dropped four points to 977.67 in Wednesday's once weekly trading session, with dealing predominantly in fixed income securities.
Turnover rose to 1,086,000 Maltese pounds ($2.8 million) from the previous week's 623,000 pounds with only 36 of 136 deals being in equities.

Business in equities totalled just over 120,400 pounds, with 95,780 shares being transacted. Of these, 81,826 were Bank of Valletta shares transacted in 28 deals for an average 124 cents each, up one cent.
There were four deals in Mid-Med Bank with 11,000 shares selling for an average 149 cents, unchanged.
Middle Sea Insurance saw one deal, with 2,000 shares selling for 120 cents each, from 122.7 cents the previous week.
Farsons ordinary shares lost one cent, with 925 shares selling for an average 49 cents. In Farsons 8.5 preference shares, 30 shares sold for 101 cents each.
Turnover on 16 issues dealt with in government bonds just topped 954,000 pounds.
There were large deals in the 6.5 percent MGS 2001 (II), the 6.9 percent MGS 2002 (II) and the 6.5 percent MGS 2000 (IV) issues, although small investors concentrated in the 7.5 percent MGS 2011.
Eight deals in Mid-Med Bank 7.25 percent unsecured loan stock 2005 amounted to 5,505 pounds, while in the 6.5 percent Gasan bonds 1998/99, four deals were transacted for 5.915 pounds.
